why: RJ-X62 (suite/cli-bundle CB-3, CB-7; pending the bundle runner, #4762): connect an AI assistant to the downloaded app. CB-7 found the in-process harness can't run it: RealJobs.check runs each step on FakeIO in this test process, which isn't inside an AfterGlow.app, so help.connect-assistant answers null, and it can't start the bundled binary, run codesign or speak MCP over stdio. So `platforms` stays empty and the harness skips it on both platforms until the bundle runner, a check that runs against the assembled .build/apps/AfterGlow.app (scripts/bundle-apps builds, signs and runs its Contents/Helpers/afterglow with --version), lands. input/launcher.suitehelp is the launcher's Help document. The job: help.connect-assistant returns the command an MCP client runs and the JSON block for clients that take one; the runner then starts that command and sends initialize and tools/list over stdio. The trap: the command points into the source tree, or at an unsigned binary that Gatekeeper stops. The assertion: the command's path is inside the bundle, quoted as one word, and starts the stdio server; codesign --verify passes on it; tools/list returns at least one tool for each of the five apps.
